coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies
coverage.found: Domestic workers are covered by the Employment Code (Domestic Workers Minimum Wages and Conditions of Employment) Order, 2023 (cited by WageIndicator; the wage figures were not confirmed). NAPSA registers employers and domestic workers through eNAPSA, which has a domestic-worker section; contributions are 5% employer plus 5% employee. Payroll returns are already rejected (K07). Weak household-employer candidate listed.

coverage.category: 2. Scrap-metal dealers
coverage.found: The Scrap Metal Dealers Act (Cap 409, Ministry of Commerce, Trade and Industry) requires a licence, a register of transactions, holding scrap for 7 days, police search power and cancellation. The licensing authority is the city/municipal/township council or the District Secretary. No 2025/2026 amendment found. Full text not machine-readable, so register contents unverified.

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: The search returned only South African, NZ and Australian regimes. No Zambian second-hand dealer or pawnbroker law found. Pawn lending may fall under Bank of Zambia non-bank lender rules (unverified).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Gold Trade Act 1912 is still listed. Zambia Monitor reports a coming revised framework with separate licences for mining, processing, trading and export of gold, to be issued by a Minerals Regulation Commission, with Bank of Zambia as sole authorised buyer. No bill number or dates. Lusaka Times (July 2026): ZCCM-IH and the Ministry of Mines are discussing gold markets; 700-1,000 cooperatives hold licences.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: Not searched specifically; no search budget was left after the other categories. No evidence found either way. Treat as unchecked.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: The Department of Veterinary Services issues stock movement permits and slaughter permits via ZamPortal. Applicants need a ZamPass digital signature, NRC and a lab/vet report. Fees are tiered by species and number (ZMW 20 for 1-4 animals, ZMW 50 for 5-50, per a third-party site). Per-movement permit, so the duty recurs.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Cattle Slaughter (Control) Act permits (inspector-granted) and the ZamPortal slaughter permit (ZMW 100/200 for immature/pregnant animals). No abattoir or butchery licensing details found.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Animal Health (Bee Keeping) Regulations, SI 94 of 2020, set import/export permits for bee products. The Zambia Residue Control Plan keeps EU honey-export listing. 2025 official push on traceability. CIFOR says no legal structure monitors beekeeping; the date of that statement is unclear.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: The Veterinary and Veterinary Para-Professions Act 2010 (Veterinary Council of Zambia licenses animal health facilities). ZAMRA registers agro-veterinary shops under the Medicines and Allied Substances Act 2013 Part III (certificate, annual returns, display, transfer; class III shops need a VCZ-certified suitably qualified person; guidelines effective Jan 2018). An amendment bill to the 2010 Act is on the Parliament site, status unclear.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: SI 18, 19 and 20 of 2018 cover charges/fees, driller licensing and groundwater/borehole regulations (notice of intention to drill, borehole registration, defective borehole reports). WARMA now requires GPS devices on rigs. Covered by known K05.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Solid Waste Regulation and Management Act No. 20 of 2018 (in force 11 April 2019) licenses solid waste service providers, operators and self-service providers, covering collection and transport. Older Cap 204 transporter regulations may still apply. No small-operator specifics, fees or portal found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Factories Act: steam and air receivers must be notified to an inspector before use and examined periodically. SI 8 of 2018 (Plant Inspection and Examination Fees) has the Commissioner notify owners by registered letter 10 days ahead. Nothing found on lifts or on private inspectors.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: NWASCO regulates utilities; a 2018 NWASCO rural framework exists. No licensing or return details for community water trusts could be found. NWASCO restored North Western utility licence June 2025 (large utility, not relevant).

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: ZEMA Pesticide and Toxic Substance licence (Environmental Management (Licensing) Regulations, SI 12 of 2013) is required to store, distribute or transport pesticides. It needs a local council trading permit, is valid 3 years, takes about 30 days and is applied for on ZamPortal with ZamPass. Add the ZAMRA agro-vet shop registration. Near K04 but a different duty.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: The Employment Code Act 2019 provides for registration of employment agencies. The old Cap 268 Part VIII had Labour Commissioner licences with a 30-day court appeal. Which provisions are in force, and the fees and process, were not confirmed.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: Cemeteries and burial permits run under the Public Health Act Cap 295 and the Local Government Act No. 2 of 2019. Lusaka City Council sells burial permits (K27 in one report) and is short of land (17,717 deaths in 2025). Private cemetery operators exist. No funeral-parlour licensing regime found.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: NGO Act 2009 (amended by Act 13 of 2020) gives a registration board and register. A 2024 NGO bill (annual returns and audit, penalties up to 3 years) had unknown status. Companies limited by guarantee also file PACRA annual returns within 3 months of year-end. Nothing on halal or kosher supervision.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: RTSA Road Service Licences (Road Traffic (Amendment) Act No. 8 of 2022): the long-term list ran 1 Sep 2023 to 31 Aug 2026, so a new cycle has just started. GPS is mandatory on PSVs. Fitness certificates are periodic (3, 4 or 12 months by class per a third-party site). Night ban 21:00-05:00. E-hailing SI 19 of 2024. RTSA's e-ZamTIS and ZamPass are used. No Zambian operator-side compliance software found.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Bank of Zambia Bureau de Change regulations (SI 38 of 2003, with 1998 weekly returns rules and a 2003 circular on capital and annual fees); current rules not confirmed. Market and street traders face ZRA presumptive tax and council or cooperative levies, with a levy dispute at the Lusaka intercity terminus. No obvious software buyer.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: The search returned only South African results for early childhood centres. No Zambian rules found for driving schools or nurseries. Tattoo and hunting not searched. Mark largely unchecked.

Medicines and Allied Substances Regulations 2017 require pharmacy annual return and re-registration. No current ZAMRA portal detail found. Candidate C09.

coverage.category: 26. Security, cleaning and manpower agencies, and the firms that hire their workers
coverage.found: Nothing new. No current Zambian private security licensing statute or 2025-26 agency rule found; only the Protected Places and Areas Act (old). Employment agency licensing not confirmed.

coverage.category: 27. Construction, mining and quarry contractors and suppliers: site registers, accreditation, local-content reports
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K01 and K02. Related find: Minerals Regulation Commission Act 2024 reserves artisanal rights to Zambian citizens or all-citizen cooperatives; 1,498 artisanal and small-scale licences issued 2023 to Aug 2025; notices of intention to cancel about 3,000 licences for non-compliance (timing unclear). Candidate C10.

coverage.category: 28. Notaries, land agents, real estate brokers and other professionals with periodic or anti-money-laundering reports
coverage.found: Estate agents are regulated by the Zambia Institute of Estate Agents under the Estate Agents Act (SI 3 of 2016 regs). A former registrar alleged about 5,000 unregistered agents (Feb 2024). Whether agents are DNFBPs with FIC reporting duties was not confirmed. Candidate C11 (weak).

coverage.category: 29. Hotels, guest houses and short-term rentals: guest registers, tourism levies
coverage.found: Tourism and Hospitality Act 2015: 1.5% tourism levy, return and remittance to ZRA by the 14th of the next month, 5% penalty for understated returns (2020 amendment, SI 121 of 2020). ZTA licences renew every 3 years; nationwide grading 1-5 stars in progress; ZTA urged licensing in Sept 2026. Candidate C05.

coverage.category: 30. Small exporters and importers facing traceability or certification rules: food, fish, timber, forest-risk commodities
coverage.found: Zambia has no national timber traceability system; an EU-funded feasibility study and roadmap for EUDR is being tendered (2026). EUDR duty usually falls on the EU operator, so small Zambian exporters mostly face buyer data requests. Honey: Zambia Residue Control Plan approved and listed for EU. No Zambian EUDR deadline for small operators confirmed. Candidate C12 (weak).

coverage.category: 31. Data protection registration (Data Protection Act 2021, Office of the Data Protection Commissioner)
coverage.found: All data controllers and processors must register; certificate is valid one year and renewal is on Form V (SI 58 of 2021). Categories are micro (max 10 staff), medium, large and individual. Online portal live; deadline 30 April 2025; offence carries ZMW 200,000 and/or 5 years (law-firm figure, differs from penalty-unit figure). No small-business support product found, only law firms. Candidate C03.

coverage.category: 32. Council trading, health and fire permits (Trades Licensing Act Cap 393, Local Government Act)
coverage.found: Councils run annual renewals of business levy, health permit, fire certificate and dangerous petroleum storage permit. Chilanga Town Council set an Oct 31, 2026 deadline for 2027 renewals with late penalties and an online payment platform (Lusaka Times, Sept 2026; page fetch blocked 403, snippet only). Renewal needs a ZRA tax clearance certificate. Deadlines are set council by council. Candidate C04.

coverage.category: 33. PACRA annual returns and beneficial ownership (Companies Act, Business Names Act)
coverage.found: PACRA deregisters entities that miss annual returns for 2 consecutive years. A Oct-Nov 2025 amnesty campaign offered one year free for businesses owing 2+ years. Beneficial ownership disclosure at annual return; penalty and deadline not found. Filing is via ZamPortal. Candidate C13 (weak, free state portal).

coverage.category: 34. Zambia Metrology Agency verification of weighing instruments (Metrology Act 6 of 2017)
coverage.found: Agency warned traders during the 2024/25 grain season that unverified or tampered scales will be seized, with fines or prosecution. Applies to traders, millers, butchers, fuel pumps (generalised, unverified). Candidate C07.

coverage.category: 35. Charcoal and forest produce permits (Forests Act 4 of 2015)
coverage.found: Wholesalers need Forestry Department permits; about K28 per 50 kg sack (2021 figure). Trucks without permits impounded (Mumbwa); minister halted cord-wood permits in Itezhi-tezhi, Mumbwa and Shibuyunji (date unclear). TI Zambia (Mar 2026) alleges fake and reused permits. Candidate C14 (weak).

coverage.category: 36. Workers' compensation (Workers' Compensation Act 10 of 1999; Domestic Workers Regulations 2021)
coverage.found: Domestic employers pay ZMW 10 per month per worker and file an annual return (schedule to SI 13 of 2021). General employer return of earnings and certificate of compliance not confirmed. Candidate C15 (household employers belong to category 1, group A's worker).

coverage.category: 37. Bank of Zambia licensed moneylenders, bureaux de change, mobile money agents
coverage.found: Budget used up on other categories.

coverage.category: 38. ZEMA environmental permits and annual returns for small quarries, workshops, waste haulers
coverage.found: Budget used up on other categories.
